monuments.name: Ponte Dom Luís I
monuments.architect: 172m Double-Deck Riveted Belgian Wrought-Iron Arch (Théophile Seyrig / Société de Willebroeck, 1886)
monuments.architecturalStyle: 172m Double-Deck Riveted Belgian Wrought-Iron Arch (Théophile Seyrig / Société de Willebroeck, 1886)
monuments.fact: Designed by Gustave Eiffel’s former partner Théophile Seyrig and inaugurated on October 31, 1886 with the longest iron arch span in the world (172m); its upper deck 60 meters above the Douro carries Metro do Porto Line D.

monuments.name: Torre dos Clérigos
monuments.architect: 75.6m Six-Story Carved Granite Baroque Campanile & Elliptical Church (Nicolau Nasoni, 1763)
monuments.architecturalStyle: 75.6m Six-Story Carved Granite Baroque Campanile & Elliptical Church (Nicolau Nasoni, 1763)
monuments.fact: Masterpiece of Italian architect Nicolau Nasoni completed in 1763; its 75.6-meter carved granite bell tower served for centuries as the maritime beacon for Port wine ships entering the Douro estuary.

monuments.name: Estação de São Bento
monuments.architect: French Beaux-Arts Granite Mansard Terminal & 20,000 Cobalt-Blue Azulejo Tiles (José Marques da Silva & Jorge Colaço, 1916)
monuments.architecturalStyle: French Beaux-Arts Granite Mansard Terminal & 20,000 Cobalt-Blue Azulejo Tiles (José Marques da Silva & Jorge Colaço, 1916)
monuments.fact: Built on the site of the 16th-century Convent of São Bento de Avé-Maria by architect José Marques da Silva and adorned with 20,000 hand-painted cobalt-blue and white Azulejo ceramic tiles by Jorge Colaço depicting Portuguese history and transport.

monuments.architect: Faceted White Concrete Polyhedron & Corrugated Glass Curtain Walls on Travertine Wave Plaza (Rem Koolhaas / OMA, 2005)

monuments.name: Sé do Porto (Porto Cathedral)
monuments.architect: Romanesque Crenellated Granite Twin-Tower Cathedral, Gothic Rose Window & Nasoni Baroque Loggia (1110–1737)
monuments.architecturalStyle: Romanesque Crenellated Granite Twin-Tower Cathedral, Gothic Rose Window & Nasoni Baroque Loggia (1110–1737)
monuments.fact: Founded around 1110 atop the ancient Roman and Suebi citadel overlooking the Douro, where King João I wed Philippa of Lancaster in 1387 to seal the Anglo-Portuguese Alliance, and enriched with silver Baroque cloister azulejos.

monuments.name: Palácio da Bolsa & Igreja de São Francisco
monuments.localName: Palácio da Bolsa & Igreja de São Francisco
monuments.architect: Neoclassical Granite Stock Exchange, Octagonal Glass Pátio das Nações & Gilded Moorish Salão Árabe (1842–1910)
monuments.architecturalStyle: Neoclassical Granite Stock Exchange, Octagonal Glass Pátio das Nações & Gilded Moorish Salão Árabe (1842–1910)
monuments.fact: Erected by the Commercial Association of Porto next to the 14th-century Gothic Church of São Francisco (famed for its gilded talha dourada woodwork), featuring the glass-domed Pátio das Nações and dazzling golden Salão Árabe.

monuments.name: Livraria Lello
monuments.architect: Neo-Gothic & Art Nouveau Tracery Facade, Stained-Glass Skylight & Crimson Forked Staircase (Xavier Esteves, 1906)
monuments.architecturalStyle: Neo-Gothic & Art Nouveau Tracery Facade, Stained-Glass Skylight & Crimson Forked Staircase (Xavier Esteves, 1906)
monuments.fact: Inaugurated on January 13, 1906 by brothers José and António Lello and engineered by Francisco Xavier Esteves, featuring a sculpted Neo-Gothic white facade and a sinuous crimson-red double staircase beneath a stained-glass motto "Decus in Labore".

monuments.name: Caves de Vinho do Porto & Serra do Pilar
monuments.localName: Caves de Vinho do Porto & Serra do Pilar
monuments.architect: Terraced Whitewashed Port Wine Lodges, Rabelo Boats & Circular Renaissance Dome of Serra do Pilar (1538–1890)
monuments.architecturalStyle: Terraced Whitewashed Port Wine Lodges, Rabelo Boats & Circular Renaissance Dome of Serra do Pilar (1538–1890)
monuments.fact: Rising in terraced terracotta-roofed ranks up the north-facing granite slopes of Vila Nova de Gaia where Port wine from the Douro Valley ages in oak vats below the UNESCO circular church and cloister of Mosteiro da Serra do Pilar.
